title: Stitchpoint transition log — midnight shift (00:00–04:00 UTC)
content:
Purpose:
This is a focused handoff / transition log for the midnight watch (00:00–04:00 UTC) after a rolling latency increase affecting inference tail latency for the hosted-api. The entry captures observed signals, tactical mitigations executed, runbook edits proposed, and follow-up actions with owners. Use this as context for the morning bridge.

High-level summary:
- Incident window: ~00:18–01:40 UTC (symptoms persisted as low-severity noise after mitigation until 03:50 UTC).
- Primary symptom: 95th/99th percentile token latency for text-generation routes rose ~2–3x on eu-west and us-central for requests >1024 tokens.
- Root cause hypothesis (working): sporadic KV cache eviction storms on the prefix cache layer combined with bursty long-context requests, which increased decoder GAN scheduling pressure and triggered autoscaler thrash on Dedicated pools.
- Impact: customer-facing error rate stayed <0.3% (no rate-limit triggered), but SLO for p99 latency breached for ~80 minutes on affected routes.

Observed signals (metrics & traces):
- spike in redis-kv-cache evictions: eviction-rate from 00:12–00:28 UTC jumped from baseline 15ev/s to ~410ev/s on cache-pool-4 (eu-west).
- queue depth on runtime-gpu-3 increased from median 2 to 14 at 00:20 UTC.
- autoscaler events: dedicated-pool-eu-west scaled up +3 nodes between 00:21–00:23 but scaled down again at 00:40 after multiple failed warmup checks.
- traces show increased KV read latency (50ms -> 480ms) and repeated cache-miss cascades.

What we did (chronological):
00:16 UTC — Pager alert (p99 latency threshold) fired. I acknowledged and started collection.
00:18 UTC — Quick triage: checked dashboards (console -> per-route latency, cache panels, autoscaler logs). Noted correlated eviction spike; opened JIRA INC-4521 (linked above).
00:22 UTC — Scoped traffic to model-family: text-gen-2/long-context; confirmed pattern across 2 AZs.
00:25 UTC — Tactical mitigations executed:
  - Disabled prefetch on rule-set prefetch-long-context-v2 for 10m (console change, targeted to eu-west).
  - Increased prefix cache memory limit for cache-pool-4 from 12GB -> 18GB (hotfix via runctl; ephemeral change to reduce eviction pressure).
  - Applied admission-control throttle to long requests (>2048 tokens) at router layer with soft-429 (5 requests/s to long-context route) to reduce burstiness.
00:40 UTC — Observed p99 decreasing toward baseline. Eviction-rate dampened to ~30ev/s.
01:05 UTC — Reenabled prefetch with a conservative worker pool (2 workers) and added telemetry tagging to track misses.
01:40 UTC — Marked incident as mitigated; moved to post-incident monitoring.

Why this likely happened (notes):
- Prefetch v2 can increase working set size; combined with recent model rollout (model-shadow: text-gen-2-long-v3) where token-allocator allocation changed, more prefixes were being pinned then evicted.
- Autoscaler warmup heuristics are too conservative for short-lived bursts: warmup failures caused nodes to scale down then up, causing oscillation and amplifying queueing.
- We lack good backpressure between prefetch and KV cache admission (prefetch floods memory, eviction storms follow).

Runbook deltas / proposed edits (short):
- Update the KV cache runbook (CONFLUENCE: SRE/Runbooks/kv-cache.md):
  1) Add a "prefetch interaction" section linking model rollout steps to cache sizing and a checklist for any prefetch toggles.
  2) Add explicit emergency knobs: a single boolean to globally disable prefetch and a per-pool memory-override playbook.
  3) Add guidance to escalate to platform-infra if autoscaler warms repeatedly fail during scale-up (include logs to collect: warmup-probe logs, kube events, node-metrics).
- Autoscaler: open ops-ticket to relax the warmup failure threshold for dedicated pools handling long-context inference (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1098).

Pending follow-ups / owners (short list):
- Diego Ramirez: create the runbook PR with the prefetch interaction section and emergency knob details — due 2027-01-05.
- Sonal Gupta: review autoscaler warmup thresholds and propose tuned parameters; run simulation with recorded 00:20 UTC traffic spike — due 2027-01-04.
- Liam O'Neill: instrument a scoped experiment to test admission-control soft-throttling under long-context bursts (small canary in eu-west) — due 2027-01-03.
- Maya Chen (me): consolidate traces and attach full debug bundle to JIRA-INC-4521 and notify the model-ops on-call to review rollout metrics for text-gen-2-long-v3.

Communications and signals to watch (for next shift):
- Watch p99 latency for routes: /v1/generate/text-gen-2/long-context, thresholds: 95ms (baseline), 220ms (warning), 500ms (pager).
- Monitor cache-pool-*/eviction-rate, prefix-cache-memory-usage and KV read latency.
- Check autoscaler events for repeated scale events in <5m windows.
- Slack: follow thread #sre-ops thread-3p2k8g for cross-team notes; ping model-ops if model-side allocations are changed.

Quick commands and artifacts collected (copy for oncoming):
- k runctl cache adjust-memory --pool cache-pool-4 --memory 18G  (executed 00:25 UTC)
- curl -s "https://console.internal/metrics?panel=kv-evictions&pool=cache-pool-4&from=00:00&to=02:00" > evictions-00-02.json
- runtime-traces: s3://redwood-debug/trace-dumps/inc-4521/trace-2026-12-31-00z.tar.gz

Lessons and longer-term actions (notes for retrospective):
- Ensure prefetch rollouts include a mandatory cache-sizing step in the model onboarding checklist.
- Add a "circuit-breaker" for prefetch where if eviction-rate > X for Y minutes, prefetch automatically disabled for the pool.
- Consider a short-lived fast-warm node tier (warm nodes with reduced warmup checks) to absorb bursts while full nodes pass warmup. Evaluate cost trade-offs.

Handoff items for incoming shift:
- Confirm JIRA-INC-4521 has the debug bundle attached and status updated to "monitoring".
- Run the query for eviction-rate for the last 4 hours and pin to the incident thread.
- If p99 > 300ms for >10m, re-apply the admission-control throttle and escalate to platform-infra.

Notes to oncoming:
- I left prefetch enabled with conservative workers (1–2) after 01:05 UTC. If you observe renewed eviction storms, disable prefetch immediately and notify model-ops.
- Watch the autoscaler warmup logs (kube events + warmup-probe) in the console; if you see repeated warmup failures during scale-up, escalate per runbook.

Raw attachments + references:
- Debug bundle: s3://redwood-debug/trace-dumps/inc-4521/
- Dashboard snapshot (png): https://console.internal/dashboards/sre/inc-4521-snapshot.png
- Runbook (draft link): CONFLUENCE: SRE/Runbooks/kv-cache.md
- JIRA: https://jira.internal/browse/INC-4521

Signed-off-by: Maya Chen (on-call)
